_comment: Mutation testing answers the question the review rounds kept asking by hand: if this guard were removed, would anything notice? On the sibling server pingen-mcp a full pass found eleven defects that eleven model rounds had not.
scope_comment: Scoped runs only — see scripts/mutate-changed.mjs. One pass of this suite is about 143 seconds, which a full file's worth of mutants turns into hours.
runner_comment: The command runner, not tap: the tests drive the server as a separate stdio child, so an in-process mutant switch never reaches the code under test and every mutant comes back NoCoverage. Hygiene is left out — it reads tracked files, so a mutant in index.js cannot change its result, and it is pure cost on every one of them.
incremental_comment: Off, and it has to be. Reuse is decided per mutant from which tests killed it, and the command runner reports the whole suite as ONE synthetic test whose identity never changes — so any test edit is invisible and the run replays old numbers in seconds.
concurrency_comment: Three, not twelve, for the same reason as the epost sibling: this suite launches real browsers, and running several at once is the configuration that fails in ways that go away when a file is run alone. Here that would be a mutant marked killed by a flake.
timeout_comment: Watch the timeout count, not the score, when changing this or concurrency. Stryker counts a timeout as detected, which scores exactly like a kill, so an allowance too tight for the machine records merely slow mutants as caught and the score inflates. On the pingen sibling, tightening it while raising concurrency took the score from 76.92% to 89.66% and the timeout count from 172 to 531 — nothing had improved.
